questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of San Marino?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the San Marino article.

questions.proof: People in San Marino speak the Italian language.

questions.prompt: Which continent is San Marino in?

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find San Marino on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find San Marino on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “It is in Southern Europe and is fully surrounded by _____ (this is called an enclave, and only the Vatican City, Lesotho and San Marino are like this).”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “surrounded”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the San Marino article.

questions.proof: It is in Southern Europe and is fully surrounded by Italy (this is called an enclave, and only the Vatican City, Lesotho and San Marino are like this).

questions.prompt: True or false: “The capital city of San Marino is Bratislava.”

hints.nudge: Read the statement slowly. Does it match what the article says, or has one word been swapped for another?
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the San Marino article, or on the Atlas.

questions.proof: The capital city of San Marino is San Marino.

questions.prompt: What money is used in San Marino?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the part of the article about the economy, or at the facts for the country.

questions.proof: The money used in San Marino is the euro.
